title: Une belle Cascade de rêve
snippet: La cascade de Wli, dans le Volta Region au Ghana, plus précisément sur la frontière Togo-Ghana, est une cascade qui prend sa source à Yikpa au Togo . Elle présente un cadre naturel, romantique avec baignade comme si vous étiez dans une piscine. Quelle beauté ?!

title: Nature's Paradise: A Must-Visit in Ghana!
snippet: Wli Waterfalls is a must-visit destination for nature lovers. Nestled in the lush greenery of the Volta Region. Calm!!

title: Awesome natural attraction. A noisy, vibrant colony of bats was the icing on the cake!
snippet: Organized under the auspices of AlphaVerse1 Travel & Tours, the entire trip and subsequent hike to the waterfalls were enlightening and very informative. Guides were capable and knowledgeable as well.
tips: Travel light to this location because the weather is just perfect -Cool and refreshing. AlphaVerse1 Travel & Tours.

title: Best waterfall Ive seen
snippet: We came here after hiking to the top of Mount Afadja, which is also great btw. So after we sweat a lot it was a great feeling to take a bath in the waterfall. The atmosphere is great, everyone enjoying it and the path to get there is also beautiful. Me and my fiancee will never forget this lovely day

title: Great hike and camping with Francis
snippet: Had a great trip with our guide Francis (0554576396). Did the hike to the middle of the waterfall and then camped down right in front of the waterfall including a bonfire and dinner.
tips: Bring water, hiking shoes and swim wear.

title: Great Day Visiting the Falls
snippet: It was a wonderful day visiting Wli Falls in Ghana.  We traveled to the Wli Falls with Happy Eagle Tours and Bless, the owner, did a great job providing a touring trip of the Volta Region.

title: Pretty views, not well communicative guide
snippet:
We booked a tour with a guy called Wisdom. In the end, he referred us to Francis, a kind guy. We clearly communicated we wanted to camp on top of the Wli Falls, but that unfortunately did not happen. We only saw the falls for a very short amount of time after we had to sleep in the village quite far away from the falls. Additionally, the guide left us waiting for quite some time on both days.

In the end, a lot of poor communication and what was planned was not delivered. Still a very pretty environment. Please, be very very clear with all communication. And normally not someone to advise against booking with someone, but it was quite disappointing to have booked with Wisdom and Francis. Another guide next time!

title: Natur pur
snippet:
Wir waren früh an der Kasse. Der Eintritt hat 80 Cedi gekostet. Außerem wird zusätzlich noch nach einer Spende gefragt. Unser Guide war ein junger Mann, der den Job nur nebenbei macht, um seine Familie zu unterstützen. Dafür, dass er keine Lust darauf hat, war er ein super Guide. Er hat viel erklärt und alle unsere Fragen beantwortet. Wir haben am Ende 50 Cedi Trinkgeld gegeben. 
An den kleinen Wasserfall waren wir nach einer leichten Wanderung nach 40 Minuten. Die Wanderung zu den upper falls war anstrengend und dauerte ca. 3h bzw. vom kleinen Wasserfall 2h - mit Fotostopp an einem Viewpoint und Pause an einer Art Altar. An beiden Wasserfällen kann man baden, aber das Wasser ist recht kalt. Direkt neben dem Kassenbereich ist ein kleines Restaurant. Nach der anstrengenden Wanderung haben wir uns für kleines Geld Fufu mit Chicken und ein Getränk gegönnt - 50 Cedi.  
Schöne Umgebung und ein sehr guter Ausgleich zu den chaotischen Städten.

title: Fascinating insight into Asante history.
snippet: very knowledgeable and informative guide, luckily coincided with when V&A London gave back on a 3 year loan some truly beautiful gold jewellery.

title: Must see if visiting Ghana and will be in Kumasi
snippet: The most recent 2 reviews I read describe this museum very accurately except there was not a gift shop that I saw. Maybe it was closed the day we went. For such a small place, there was a lot of history. I wish I could have taken pictures of the board that showed the history of the Asante royals and what happened to each of them. The British museum had currently loaned some of the artifacts they themselves admit they had stolen, back to Ghana. But, apparently they plan to take those back to England in a few months so you better get over there and see them while you can! However, the US has permanently returned the artifacts they had acquired, to the Ghanians. So, those you should be able to see even if you don't come for a while, There is more cool stuff in each room and plenty of interesting history. The Ashante royal family is also one of few African tribal kingdoms the British royals acknowledge and invited to the Queen's funeral. So, I learned a lot about this tribe from this museum.
tips: Don't come late in the day near rush hour. We found this area of town very difficult to get out of when we left when the museum closed.

title: Asante history in a nutshell
snippet:
While in Kumasi, I visited the Manhyia Palace Museum. The tour started with a short video on the history of the Asantes (yes this is the correct spelling). I learned about the rise of the Asante kingdom, the Asantehene, the Queen Mother and the resilience of the Asante warriors. This really set the pace for the rest of the tour which was quite informative and educational. 

Our tour guide led us through room after room and explained the significance (and importance) of each artifact such as original furniture, thrones, wax figures, gold ornaments and even a working refrigerator from 1974!  However, please note that pictures and recordings are not allowed. 

Overall I left with a feeling of cultural awareness and empowerment; but most importantly, a connection to and an appreciation of these majestic people which I descended from. 

Tip - Schedule your visit for the same day of the Akwasidae Festival which is an experience in itself!
tips: The Akwasidae festival is held at the palace every 6th Sunday. Try to plan your visit for that day so you experience this as well.

title: Ashante Museum: The Jamaican Connection!
snippet:
The Manhyia Palace Museum is located in Kamsi, Ghana. The grounds of the museum and Palace were beautiful. On the grounds were several peacocks, art on the walls, a Peace Bell and a very large Indian Rubber tree.  As we entered the museum there was an area where you saw a video on the the history and culture of the Ashante Kingdom.

What stuck with me the most was that the royal succession, in Ghana, is matrilineal. Which means that the family line is traced through the mother. 

The colors of the Ashante tribe are gold, black, and green. My aha moment came when I realized the the colors of Jamaica are the same, and Jamaicans can trace their lineage to Ghana from the transatlantic slave trade. 

The museum has a gift shop. The only problem was that you cannot take pictures in the museum only outside on the grounds. Good day!

title: Bardzo ciekawe muzeum .
snippet: Głównym obiektem kompleksu muzealnego jest Pałac Manhyia. Tu mieli swą siedzibę królowie Królestwa Aszanti . Zgromadzono tu oryginalne sprzęty z wyposażenia pałacu i dużo cennych dla kultury i tradycji  Aszanti "skarbów". Niestety pod żadnym pozorem nie wolno wewnątrz robić zdjęć . Zresztą na zewnątrz pałacu też są one w zasadzie zabronione . W niewielkim parku obok  zwraca uwagę potężny , ponad stuletni figowiec i swobodnie spacerujące pawie . Tam także ustawiony jest [ w roku 2019 ] pamiątkowy dzwon . Poświęcony jest zmarłemu rok wcześniej byłemu sekretarzowi generalnemu ONZ Kofi Annanowi który urodził się w Kumasi . W muzealnym sklepie jest spory wybór afrykańskiego rękodzieła , magnesów i innych pamiątek w rozsądnych cenach .

title: History told by its own people
snippet: Was more of group to friends trip. I love their gifts shop and the pricing is moderate. You get to learn a lot about the Ashanti history and not through a white man’s lens but from the people themselves which gives it a different perspective if you have studied Ashanti history in school. I would say it is a must for all who visit Kumasi to pass through.

title: Führung im Schnelldurchlauf
snippet:
Nur wegen dem Palast würde ich nicht nach Kumasi. Der Eintritt kostet 100 Cedi. Die Führung dauert ca. 30 Min. Ein Einführungsvideo habe ich nicht gesehen. Man darf keine Fotos machen.
Es war zwar interessant etwas über die Ashanti Geschichte zu lernen, aber mir war die Führung zu kurz - der Guide hat alles im Schnelldurchlauf erklärt. Auch draußen muss man genau aufpassen, wie weit man das Gelände betritt. Es gibt noch einen Souvenirshop mit günstigen Preisen (Kartenzahlung möglich).

title: wer sich für Kultur interessiert, ein unbedingtes MUSS.
snippet: Hoch interessant, einen Enblick in die Ashanti Kultur zu bekommen. Die Führung durch einen Museumsangestellten war gut gemacht, und informativ. Leider ein absolutes fotografier Verbot.

title: Palace Tour
snippet: It's a brief but very informative tour of the palace which was built by the British after they had burnt his other one down and sent the king into exile. It's a sad story of the brutality used on the people in order to subdue them, but it's also a glimpse into the organisation and community-mindedness of this ancient kingdom. Well worth a visit.

title: Amazing History
snippet: The Manhyia Palace boasts of the rich culture of the Ashanti kingdom. it is an amazing place to learn about the struggles of the people of Ghana and the Ashantis.

title: The guide makes the visit worthwhile
snippet: Small museum hosting some interesting cultural treasures. It is painful to see that the objects on display are gathering dust and not protected well enough from visitors and weather. Authorities should invest in climate control to maintain the cultural treasures it holds. In this case, the museum guide makes all the difference in terms of the experience, sharing interesting information and facts about the various objects on display.

title: One not to miss in Kumasi!
snippet:
Absolutely excellent museum. Small but perfectly formed as they say! It houses many asante artifacts from the olden days which all together tell a very interesting story. 

The guide who showed us round was very knowledgeable and informative.

title: Compact but good
snippet: Never judge a museum by it’s size. This one is small but packed full of good information on the Ashanti empire. Well worth a stop.

title: A must visit location
snippet: Great place. A guided tour is included as part of the price and the guide Keane was great - thorough and very knowledgeable. This place is definitely worth a visit to learn more about Ashanti history and customs.

title: A small gem in the Cultural Center
snippet: This small building is in the Cultural Center.  It includes items of crafts and historical items.  Our guide was very knowledgeable.

title: A Must Visit
snippet: The museum is an excellent place for discovering Ashante royal traditions, history of the Ashante people and culture. It's a small museum, so it won't take long, but the staff there give you a wealth of information. If I had the time, I would have gone back for a second visit, perhaps next time I'm in Kumasi. Definitely worth visiting.

title: Fantastic museum on Ashanti History
snippet: They have great items here which are worth seeing and the guides are helpful. This is the location of the fake golden stool as well as other items of value and note

title: Knowledge is Power
snippet:
I was overwhelmed with delight as I learned a lot with a stop at Ghana’s National Cultural Center where I was awash with pride learning about the Ashanti Kings and Queen mothers, their rise, fall and rise again from a knowledgeable and enthusiastic guide. The brave Queen who took on the British at the age of sixty was my favorite.
The place replica is small but gives you an idea of what the real palace is like. It is full of ancient artifacts that the British hadn't stolen and the Ashanti people are proud at preserving their history. 
If you love history told from a non-European narrative this is a must do.

title: Compact museum but comprehensive explanation
snippet: A guided tour is included in the admission fee of 10 GHS for foreigners. My guide, Adwoa, is very good. Well worth a visit if you are visiting the National Cultural Centre.

title: History is Good!
snippet: This is an excellent place to visit to gain knowledge of the traditions and history of the Ashanti Royalty. My guide was extremely knowledgeable and answered all of my questions.

title: Aburi Botanical Gardens, established in 1890, is a historic, scenic, and affordable nature escape located 32km from Accr
snippet: The Aburi Botanical Gardens, established in 1890, is a historic,135-year-old, colonial-era garden in Ghana's Eastern Region offering a peaceful, cooler alternative to Accra. Visitors typically enjoy the stunning "Avenue of Royal Palms," diverse tree species, and guided tours highlighting medicinal plants and history. While cherished for its natural beauty, many visitors note the facility is largely neglected, with dilapidated infrastructure and limited on-site dining.

title: Nature at its best
snippet: One of the hidden gems in Africa. Went there for my anniversary celebration. The greenery is amazing and the history behind the trees unbelievable

title: Natur super, Tiere absolut unerträglich
snippet: Da wir an Ostermontag hier waren, war der Park sehr gut besucht, überall waren Familien, die Picknicks hatten, die Kinder haben gespielt, überall wurde Musik gemacht. Trotzdem konnte man die Schönheit des Parks sehen. Was aber gar nicht geht, ist der sogenannte Minizoo. Hier werden Tiere auf die erbärmlichste Art gehalten. Für uns war es unerträglich, dies anzuschauen. Dieser Zoo ist in einem Botanischen Garten absolut nicht notwendig.

title: Lovely botanical garden
snippet: Visited the botanical gardens. Yaw was our guide and he did a very good job. The gardens are extensive so we didn't get round the whole area. The information given was extremely interesting.  We were short on time and wanted to visit the waterfall so we cut this short. Well worth a visit and if you get a guide then it can be really useful.
tips: It's much cooler up there.

title: Tree variety
snippet: Beautiful trees but lots of rubbish everywhere which rather spoiled the effect. Main path with tall palms is grand and calm

title: It is cool and calm to visit here. for recreational purpose and vacation... I'll recommend 10/10 everyone
snippet: I love nature and the fact that this garden has so much to share and enlightenment… thank you to our great guide Martin! Very patient and full of knowledge. Next time I’ll be prepared to embark on the jungle trail… says the soldier in me! ☺️ but in this garden you’ll find cooking spices and medicinal trees and even a “snake tree” 😳… peaceful grounds, a lovely place to pray and meditate and lots of trees rather giant size or unique stature. I’ll definitely visit again. The little shops are also nice to visit …

title: Peaceful Aburi Botanical Gardens
snippet:
Oasis of calm so close to busy Accra. We had one of the official garden guides who spent an hour explaining the main attractions there. He was great, very engaging and explained what certain plants were used for and how to recognise them as well as the history of the garden.  

The gardens themselves are an interesting mix of plants from around the world, nicely kept paths and you can easily spend an hour walking on flat paths, although there are some stepped routes if you want to ramble more.

title: Average
snippet: Very difficult stone paths are uneven  I agree, it's pretty, but not well maintained. it felt like a zoo without animals to me. Just average.

title: Beautiful, tranquil setting with excellent guides
snippet: Quiet, lovely location. The weather is cooler, the atmosphere is serene. Our guide Quartey was excellent, and we learnt about the history of the Botanical Gardens as well as a number of fantastic trees, plants and shrubs. Seeing and tasting cocoa fruit was a great experience, and there were food and souvenir stalls with a delicious fruit salad, freshly made and beautifully served.

title: What a let down
snippet: Poorly maintained tourist attraction. Moss covered poorly maintained paths, overgrown lawns, weeds everywhere, rusty signage, dilapidated buildings.  We were charged 20 Cedis which is twice tourist price and 4 times local residents entrance fee. What are they using the money for? Where is the management or tourist board, who is accountable for false advertising to tourists? The staff blame the government for lack of investment but they sit around chatting and have no pride in their country, just try to guide you to the souvenirs. Left very disappointed as had been looking forward to a relaxing walk through a beautiful botanical garden but it’s a dump.

title: Don’t miss the falls!
snippet:
Thoroughly enjoyed this trip. The falls were the highlight as we went during the rainy season when they were in full force - incredible place. Really enjoyed the botanical gardens as well. Make sure to take some small notes to tip the villagers at the Umbrella rock. 

Great communication from our guide and driver, and despite someone driving into the back of our car, they kept calm and we always felt safe. Highly recommend!

title: Search for another tour
snippet:
I am giving this tour three stars based primarily on my interaction with the tour owner. The night before the tour, I confirmed my 7:00 a.m. hotel pickup with the operator via WhatsApp. The next morning, at 7:05 a.m., I called three times with no answer. I then contacted Viator, who also received no response and stated they would follow up by email.

At 7:44 a.m., the operator finally contacted me to apologize, explaining that he had misplaced his phone and that the driver was waiting at the wrong hotel. After exchanging messages and providing proof of my reservation showing the correct hotel, I was told the driver would arrive within five minutes—which, due to Accra traffic, turned into about 30 minutes.

While I did not expect a full refund, I did feel some compensation for the delay and confusion was warranted. I was offered $17 USD, which I ultimately declined out of frustration.

The tour guide, Isaac, communicated that he was stuck in traffic and arrived around 8:30 a.m. He was very apologetic, friendly, and made the rest of the day enjoyable. He was engaging, assisted with photos and translations, drove safely, and provided bottled water.

Although I would not recommend this tour due to the owner’s lack of communication, the Botanical Gardens and Boti Waterfalls are definitely worth visiting—just perhaps with a different company at a better price.

Tip: Even if you don’t plan to swim, bring a swimsuit for photos in the water. There is a changing area available.

title: Nice tour in Ghana's country side
snippet:
The nature garden was interesting.  Learned alot about the fauna.  We were allowed to handle some of the leaves, bark, fruit and seeds. That was very informative as well.  
Really enjoyed the coco farm tour. Learning the difference between Ghana cocoa and South America's. Being able to taste the different cocoa was a plus. Purchased black soap n chocolates.  Too bad Boti Falls were dry but we did Asenema which were quite refreshing.  We finished with a nice traditional Ghanian lunch that was delicious. 
Kofi our tour guide was very informative and polite. He pointed out many sites along the way. He was very accommodating in the morning at pick-up.
He answered all of our questions.

title: Would book with them again!
snippet: Isaac and Emmanuel were excellent guides on this tour. Isaac was knowledgeable and accommodating and Emmanuel was able to get us to and from safe and sound especially when going through areas with difficult roads. They were professional and I felt safe traveling as a solo woman. The tours were amazing and I would recommend anyone interested to book with them. Thank you guys for an amazing time!
tips: Definitely being water and wear comfortable shoes.

title: Simply Amazing
snippet:
Our tour was amazing! First to the botanical garden where we took so many pictures and the guide was so knowledgeable then we were off to the cocoa farm.  Both were amazing but NOTHING can compare to the Boti Falls!  
I was afraid of the steps but I was able to concur them down and back up!
The  falls were peaceful and beautiful and simply amazing!
My husband and I took so many pictures for memories of Ghana!
So happy we booked this tour and Michael was awesome!  He stopped and got us local snacks, water and fruit on the way home!
Overall we would give this a 10 rating!!!!!
